newsitem.title: CANADA: Talisman making life difficult for CanOxy.
newsitem.headline: Talisman making life difficult for CanOxy.

text.p: A move by Talisman Energy Inc to hold onto 10.3 percent of Wascana Energy Inc stock has left questions over whether it planned to make Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd's acquisition of the Regina-based oil producer as difficult as possible.
CanOxy said on Tuesday it succeeded in acquiring all shares of Wascana by the midnight Pacific time deadline except those held by Talisman and its corporate ally, Altamira Management Ltd.
CanOxy spokesman Kevin Finn, whose offer for Wascana was valued at C$2-billion, played down Talisman's move, saying the takeover may just take more time than the company had planned.
Finn said Talisman had given no indication by late Monday whether it planned to tender the stock.
"Because we don't have 90 percent it will take us a little longer. We won't be able to do the statutory acquisition, but that's life -- we will do it," he said.
Under Canadian regulations, companies must have at least 90 percent of a takeover target's shares before it can undertake a compulsory acquisition of the remainder.
A Talisman spokesman was not immediately available for comment.

Talisman, which opened the bidding for Wascana with a C$1.8 billion cash-and-stock offer in February, has been highly critical of Wascana's board of directors, which it said kept it out of the confidential data room during the bid process.
Talisman chief executive Jim Buckee said in a conference call last week that, by closing the door on his firm, Wascana's board took away the potential for a richer takeover bid.
He also suggested that legal action may be in the offing.
"I find it hard to believe that they have much of a claim, given that they were the ones that elected not to participate in the process that Wascana set up," Finn said.
"They certainly could have had access to the data room had they signed a confidentiality agreement. They were looking for special treatment."
Talisman last week let its offer expire without raising it.
